I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` workflow because this is a cross-language rename investigation. I’ll keep this read-only and use the supplied finding as the starting point to map the rename surface and adjacent contract drift.

The skill is stored at the evaluation workspace level rather than this fixture runner, so I’m loading it from its declared path and then I’ll inspect the relevant Python and TypeScript contexts.

The local built CLI is available. I’m running the broad fixture scan plus per-file context checks now; that should distinguish the actual rename surface from unrelated warnings in the same three-file repo.

The broad scan confirms the rename is not just symbol-level: the name is embedded in function names, URL paths, parameters, and the plan model’s documentation. The per-file checks also found no likely tests, so I’m doing one literal-name inventory to make sure the four unscanned manifest/config files do not hide another occurrence.

No changes were made. `crimes scan . --all` identified the core object as the **tenant** concept:

> The “tenant” concept is called `team` in Python and `workspace` in TypeScript, across 3 files. Preferred form: `organization`.

Rename surface:

- Python uses `team`:
  - [plans.py](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:11>) — plan-model documentation.
  - [routes.py](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/routes.py:10>) — `/api/teams` routes, `get_team`, `create_team`, `team_seats`, `change_team_plan`, and `team_id`.

- TypeScript uses `workspace`:
  - [workspace-client.ts](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:12>) — filename, `Workspace` interface, `getWorkspace`, `createWorkspace`, `workspaceSeats`, `changeWorkspacePlan`, comments, and `/api/workspaces` URLs.

The rename should therefore cover all three files, including public identifiers, route paths, client URLs, `team_id`, comments/docstrings, and probably `workspace-client.ts` itself. `Plan.TEAM` should not be mechanically renamed: it appears to be a subscription tier rather than the tenant object.

There are also contract problems to resolve alongside the rename:

- `POST /api/workspaces` has no backend route; the backend exposes `POST /api/teams`.
- The client uses `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan`, while the backend declares `POST /api/teams/{team_id}/plan`.
- The plan sets disagree: Python has `free | pro | team | scale`; TypeScript has `free | pro | enterprise`. This is the scan’s only high-severity finding.
- `getWorkspace` is flagged as misleading because it performs network I/O; a rename such as `fetchOrganization` would address both concerns.

`crimes context` found no likely tests for any of the three files. The scan excluded three JSON files and one TOML file, but a literal inventory found no additional `team`, `workspace`, or `organization` occurrences in them.
